title: Configure tsconfig.json for ESM + Node.js 22
description: Create the TypeScript compiler configuration for the project. The config must support ESM (NodeNext module system), Node.js 22 runtime targets, strict type checking, and a separate tsconfig for the bin/ entry point. Use composite builds to support both src/ and bin/ outputs.
acceptanceCriteria: A separate tsconfig for bin/ exists or bin/ is included in the root tsconfig
tsc --noEmit passes with no errors on a minimal src/index.ts file

steps.details: Create tsconfig.json at project root with compilerOptions: { module: 'NodeNext', moduleResolution: 'NodeNext', target: 'ES2022', strict: true, outDir: 'dist', rootDir: 'src', declaration: true, declarationMap: true, sourceMap: true, esModuleInterop: true, skipLibCheck: true }
Add 'include': ['src/**/*'] and 'exclude': ['node_modules', 'dist', '**/*.test.ts'] to the root tsconfig.json.

Create tsconfig.bin.json at project root that extends the root tsconfig but overrides rootDir to cover both src/ and bin/. Set 'rootDir': '.' and include both 'src/**/*' and 'bin/**/*'. Or alternatively, include bin/ in the root tsconfig by setting rootDir to '.'.
Run `npm install --save-dev typescript @types/node`. This is needed before tsc can run. Use TypeScript 5.x.

steps.description: Create a minimal src/index.ts to verify compilation
steps.details: Create src/index.ts with a single export: `export const version = '0.1.0'`. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` to verify zero TypeScript errors. The noEmit flag checks types without writing output files.

technicalNotes: NodeNext module resolution requires .js extensions in import statements even for .ts source files — this is a common gotcha
composite: true enables project references which speeds up incremental builds
skipLibCheck: true is recommended to avoid errors in third-party type definitions
